paragraphs: This is a production line position that reliably converts bulk, liquid, or individual products into storable and shippable finished goods; the core is getting cycle time, sealing, weight, labeling, and batch right at the same time. Precise occupational wages for China are currently unavailable.
Suited to those who can continuously verify feed, containers, seals, counts, and labels at the equipment's cycle rate and are willing to document short stoppages and defects clearly.
If you tend to skip first-article checks, records, or guard checks during repetitive work, or would handle jams by hand, the quality and safety friction on this path will be very high.

Start with a simulated batch: draw the process from feeding to palletizing, fill in a first-article record, and write the escalation action for mislabeling, underfill, poor sealing, and jams separately.

Complete label counting and finished-product quality checks, keep label batch numbers and run records, and hand over anomalies.

Jam handling, stoppage reset, deviation release, and maintenance authorization are controlled by accountable personnel, and AI can only give restricted suggestions.

Entry starts with identifying packaging materials, products, equipment status, batches, and labels, and practicing pre-start checks, first-article confirmation, and standard records.

Sample one: create a changeover verification checklist covering line clearance, materials, containers, label templates, metering, sealing, and reject testing. Paper problem statement: AC01 order batch L1 and label L2; AD01 is the same batch, the fictional specification is 500±5 grams, the record is 493 grams, the reject column is blank, and the summary reads qualified. Follow only the given rule: batch numbers must match, 495—505 grams includes the boundary, and unknown is not a pass; list the deviations and persons to verify, and do not operate equipment or real products.

Sample two: create a batch anomaly packet linking weight trends, mislabel photos, stoppage time, isolation quantity, and restart signatures. Reference: AC01 keeps the L1/L2 original values, lists the mislabel for quality review, and does not change the batch number without authorization; AD01493 below 495 is a paper underfill, and the unknown rejection conflicts with the qualified summary, so it is not marked released. The work submits a two-line deviation table and a simulated escalation draft, listing the original values, quantities to verify, responsible person, and correction records; it does not infer whole-batch defect counts or adjust machine parameters.

entries: Days 1—2: draw the material path for feeding, filling, sealing, labeling, inspection, and boxing.
Days 3—4: fill in the pre-start and first-article tables and design reviewable records for the four defect types.

AC/AD addendum: Day 1 copy the fictional inputs and the 495—505 rule, inclusive of both endpoints; Days 2—4 create the two-line batch and weight deviation table and the draft that keeps original values pending verification, using only paper simulation without performing line clearance.
Day 5: simulate changeover line clearance and confirm that old materials and old labels do not enter the new batch.
Days 6—7: simulate jams and weight drift, and write the sequence for stoppage, isolation, escalation, and restart.

AC/AD addendum: Days 5—7 submit the two-line table, escalation draft, and simulated quality review feedback and corrections; the rejection quantity is still unknown as not given, and no real filling, parameter adjustment, jam clearing, or release is performed.

career_risk_cards.heading: Machine guarding, jam, and batch risks

risks.mitigation: Stop per procedures and notify the responsible person for guard anomalies, without removing guards on your own.
risks.scenario: Operation continues despite a guard anomaly on conveying or sealing moving parts.
risks.title: Pinch and entanglement

risks.consequence: May cause sudden movement, crushing, or cuts.
risks.mitigation: Handle per safe shutdown and escalation procedures, and do not reach past guards to make emergency repairs.
risks.scenario: Reaching past guards to clear jams to restore output.
risks.title: Improper jam clearing

risks.consequence: May be injured by unexpected start-up or energy release.
risks.mitigation: Trained authorized personnel isolate and verify per the applicable energy control procedure.
risks.scenario: Treating the stop button as if all hazardous energy were isolated.
risks.title: Hazardous energy

risks.consequence: May harm identification traceability and batch quality.
risks.mitigation: Verify orders, material templates, and first articles, isolate suspected cross-batch material, and hand it to quality for decision.
risks.scenario: Old labels or materials mix into the new batch after changeover.
risks.title: Mislabeling and cross-batch mixing

risks.mitigation: Observe workstations, weight rotation, and assist devices, and report to the on-site manager.
risks.scenario: Repetitive lifting and twisting with unverified workstations and assist arrangements.
risks.title: Repetitive lifting

risks.affected_roles: Operators, quality personnel, and batch recipients
risks.consequence: May leave personnel safety or product deviations out of control.
risks.mitigation: Authorized personnel verify fault clearance, guards, rejection, and first article and record the restart decision.
risks.scenario: Restarting before guards, rejection, or first article are verified.
risks.title: Wrong restart
